capabilities.target: payments.issue_refund (any order, any amount up to the order total)

instructions.note: The prompt directs the agent to process refunds and to use its own judgment on partial refunds, without narrowing refund criteria or authority checks.
The design relies on prompt text for refund decision behavior and explicitly says not to ask for confirmation, with no structural approval or provenance control described.
Use your judgment on partial refunds leaves decision thresholds and acceptable rationale undefined.

controls.name: SSO-authenticated staff request channel
controls.decay_rationale: Authentication of the requesting staff channel does not decay with model capability, but it authenticates origin only and does not constrain refund authority or attribution.

controls.name: Payments processor transaction log
controls.decay_rationale: The processor log persists regardless of model capability, but it is detective only and lacks staff requester attribution.

controls.name: Attributable refund request provenance bound to each refund action
controls.decay_rationale: A structural binding of staff identity and request reason to each refund would not decay with model capability and would restore attributable action provenance.

controls.name: Least-privilege refund credential scoped to requester authority and approved refund limits
controls.decay_rationale: A scoped credential would constrain refund authority at the payments processor and would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate for irreversible refunds
controls.decay_rationale: A per-refund raw-action approval would remain effective regardless of model capability if each request is reviewed individually.

controls.name: Refund request retention longer than chat deletion window
controls.decay_rationale: Retaining request records does not decay with model capability and improves later investigation, but by itself does not prevent an improper refund.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): trusted staff request can trigger irreversible refunds through a shared service account broader than the requester

attack_path.note: Agent reads order history and payment details to choose refund amount.
Agent issues an irreversible refund using a shared service account.

forecast.watch_signal: New broader refund entitlements, larger refund limits, or expanded payment actions granted to the shared service account.

evidence.observation: The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool.
The prompt directs the agent to check the order and then issue the refund, and to use its own judgment on partial refunds without confirmation.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Replace the shared service account with a least-privilege credential or authorization check that enforces requester-specific refund authority and amount limits at the payment processor.
Require raw-action human approval for refunds above a defined threshold or for all partial refunds until authority and policy checks are implemented structurally.

findings.title: Missing property: refund actions are not attributable to the requesting staff member

forecast.watch_signal: Longer retention gaps, more unattended refund volume, or continued deletion of request context before settlement and review.

evidence.observation: The processor log records the service account, the amount, and the order, but not which staff member asked or why.
The agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day.

recommendations.action: Bind each refund action to immutable provenance containing staff identity, request identifier, and rationale, and store it in an audit record the model cannot alter.
Retain refund request records beyond the current 7-day chat deletion window and link them to processor log entries for review and dispute handling.

stride_coverage.rationale: The artifacts do not describe configuration change controls, tool definition integrity, or whether the agent can modify its own runtime.
No egress or disclosure capability is declared in the reviewed design; the described actions are order read and refund issuance only.
The artifacts do not say whether step limits, spend caps, rate limits, or loop-prevention controls exist for refund processing.
The artifacts confirm the log exists but do not describe tamper-evidence, write protections, or retention controls for the processor log.
The artifacts do not describe who can read processor log contents or whether confidential payment data in the log is access-controlled.
The artifacts do not say whether logging can fail closed, be exhausted, or be rate-limited during bursts of refund activity.

rating.rationale: Present design evidence shows one moderate path finding for shared-account refund authority and one high property finding for missing attributable provenance on irreversible refunds. No declared preventive control restores attribution or constrains the refund sink. Missing runtime artifacts for rate limits, approval workflow, and authorization policy reduce confidence on some STRIDE pairs, but not on the two recorded findings.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, source code, IaC, or detailed runtime configuration was provided, so approval gates, spend caps, rate limits, and authorization checks could not be verified.
No explicit policy defining authorized refund amounts, requester roles, or exception handling was provided, so judgment about refund authority was based on the prompt and runtime notes only.
